mechanism_narrative: A GDP level exceeding $15,000 billion (2017 chained dollars) indicates robust economic expansion, generating elevated corporate earnings expectations that produce positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns through sustained equity demand.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 exceeds $15,000 billion.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate decline below 8.0% over three months signals tightening labor market conditions, increasing consumer spending capacity and corporate revenue growth, which drives positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE falls below 8.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) increases exceeding 0.5% in one month indicate synchronized manufacturing and construction sector strength, generating positive S&P 500 20-day returns through elevated capital expenditure expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both rise > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO and HOUST both rise > 0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), a consumer spending decline below the 12-month moving average signals weakening demand, triggering negative S&P 500 20-day returns due to reduced corporate revenue forecasts.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances during FEDFUNDS > 4.5% when RSAFS declines below 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: Payroll employment growth exceeding 100,000 jobs in one month indicates strengthening labor market conditions, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, which produces positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS increases by >100k jobs.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL exceeding 3.0% annualized inflation rate signals persistent price pressures, prompting aggressive Federal Reserve tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 60-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0% annualized.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous retail sales (RSAFS) and industrial production (INDPRO) increases exceeding 0.5% in one month indicate strong consumer demand and manufacturing output, generating positive S&P 500 20-day returns through elevated corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and INDPRO both rise > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS and INDPRO both rise > 0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: In post-shock recovery phases (INDPRO below 12-month moving average), a rebound above the 12-month moving average signals manufacturing sector stabilization, generating positive S&P 500 20-day returns through renewed capital investment cycles.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO rebounds above 12-month MA during post-shock recovery.
